subject.title: [Feature]: Discord self-profile updates (strict bot-only scope for nickname/avatar/status)

question: Should OpenClaw add a Discord bot self-profile mutation action, and should it use the existing `set-profile` action pattern or a new Discord-specific `self-profile` name?
rationale: The current code has internal presence mutation and a generic channel profile-action pattern, but adding Discord nickname/avatar mutation changes a bot-credential-backed identity control surface and public config/tool semantics that automation should not choose alone.

options.title: Approve a gated Discord profile action
options.body: Add a Discord plugin-owned profile mutation action with default-off gating, explicit account/guild selection, strict self-only checks, owner/requester authorization, avatar validation, docs, tests, and live Discord proof.

options.title: Limit Discord to existing presence controls
options.body: Keep `setPresence`, static presence, and autoPresence as the only supported identity-adjacent Discord controls, and reject nickname/avatar mutation for now.

options.title: Fold into broader identity override design
options.body: Defer this issue behind the per-channel identity work at https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/41459 if maintainers want one coherent Discord visible-identity model.

recommendation.title: Approve a gated Discord profile action
recommendation.body: Add a Discord plugin-owned profile mutation action with default-off gating, explicit account/guild selection, strict self-only checks, owner/requester authorization, avatar validation, docs, tests, and live Discord proof.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the merged adjacent Discord auto-presence work and are the clearest current routing candidate for the Discord presence/profile behavior decision.
